paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Technological changes brought dramatic new options to Americans living in the 1990s. During this decade new forms of entertainment, commerce, research, and communication became commonplace in the U. S. The driving force behind much of this change was a(n) 26 popularly known as the Internet.
paragraphs.translationZh: 技术变革为 20 世纪 90 年代的美国人带来了巨大的新选择。在这十年中，新的娱乐、商业、研究和通信形式在美国变得司空见惯。这种变化背后的驱动力是众所周知的互联网创新。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Internet was developed during the 1970s by the Department of Defense. In the case of an attack, military advisers suggested the 27 of being able to operate one computer from another terminal. In the early days, the Internet was used mainly by scientists to communicate with other scientists. The Internet 28 under government control until 1984.
paragraphs.translationZh: 互联网是 20 世纪 70 年代由国防部开发的。在发生攻击的情况下，军事顾问提出了能够从另一个终端操作一台计算机的优势。早期，互联网主要由科学家用来与其他科学家进行交流。直到 1984 年，互联网仍处于政府控制之下。

paragraphs.sourceText: One early problem faced by Internet users was speed. Phone lines could only transmit information at a 29 rate. The development of fiber-optic(光纤) cables allowed for billions of bits of information to be received every minute. Companies like Intel developed faster microprocessors, so personal computers could process the 30 signals at a more rapid rate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 互联网用户早期面临的问题之一是速度。电话线只能以有限的速率传输信息。光纤电缆的发展使得每分钟可以接收数十亿比特的信息。像英特尔这样的公司开发了更快的微处理器，因此个人计算机可以以更快的速度处理传入的信号。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the early 1990s, the World Wide Web was developed, in large part, for 31 purposes. Corporations created home pages where they could place text and graphics to sell products. Soon airline tickets, hotel 32 ,and even cars and homes could be purchased online. Universities 33 research data on the Internet, so students could find 34 information without leaving their dormitories. Companies soon discovered that work could be done at home and 35 online, so a whole new class of telecommuters began to earn a living from home offices unshaven and wearing pajamas(睡衣).
paragraphs.translationZh: 20 世纪 90 年代初，万维网的开发很大程度上是为了商业目的。公司创建了主页，可以在其中放置文本和图形来销售产品。很快，机票、酒店预订，甚至汽车和房屋都可以在网上购买。大学将研究数据发布到互联网上，这样学生足不出户就可以找到有价值的信息。公司很快发现工作可以在家完成并在线提交，因此全新一类远程办公人员开始在不刮胡子、穿着睡衣的家庭办公室谋生。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Health Benefits of Knitting
paragraphs.translationZh: 针织对健康的好处

paragraphs.sourceText: A) About 15 years ago, I was invited to join a knitting group. I agreed to give it a try.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 大约15年前，我受邀加入一个编织小组。我同意尝试一下。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) My mother had taught me to knit at 15, and I knitted in class throughout college and for a few years thereafter. Then decades passed without my touching a knitting needle. But within two Mondays in the group, I was hooked, not only on knitting but also on crocheting(钩织)，and I was on my way to becoming a highly productive crafter.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 我母亲在 15 岁时就教我编织，整个大学期间以及此后的几年我都在课堂上编织。然后几十年过去了，我没有碰过一根织针。但在小组的两个星期一内，我不仅迷上了针织，还迷上了钩织，并且我正在成为一名高产的工匠。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) I’ve made countless baby blankets, sweaters, scarves, hats, caps for newborns. I take a knitting project with me everywhere, especially when I have to sit still and listen. As I discovered in college, when my hands are busy, my mind stays focused on the here and now.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 我为新生儿制作了无数的婴儿毛毯、毛衣、围巾、帽子、帽子。我到处都带着编织项目，尤其是当我必须安静地坐着倾听时。正如我在大学时发现的那样，当我的双手忙碌时，我的思想会专注于此时此地。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. It seems, too, that I’m part of a national renewal of interest in needle and other handicrafts(手工艺). The Craft Yarn Council reports that a third of women ages 25-35 now knit or crochet. Even men and schoolchildren are swelling the ranks, among them my friend’s three small grandsons. Last April, the council created a “Stitch Away Stress” campaign in honor of National Stress Awareness Month. Dr. Herbert Benson, a pioneer in mind/body medicine and author of The Relaxation Response, says that the repetitive action of needlework can induce a relaxed stats like that associated with meditation(沉思)and yoga. Once you get beyond the initial learning curve, knitting and crocheting can lower heart rate and blood pressure.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 看来我也是全国人民对针和其他手工艺品兴趣复兴的一部分。工艺纱线委员会报告称，25-35 岁的女性中有三分之一现在从事针织或钩编工作。就连男人和学童也在不断壮大，其中包括我朋友的三个小孙子。去年四月，该委员会发起了一项“消除压力”活动，以纪念全国压力意识月。身心医学先驱、《放松反应》一书的作者赫伯特·本森博士表示，重复的针线活可以引发放松状态，就像冥想和瑜伽那样。一旦超越了最初的学习曲线，针织和钩编可以降低心率和血压。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) But unlike meditation, craft activities result in tangible and often useful products that can enhance self-esteem. I keep photos of my singular accomplishments on my cellphone to boost my spirits when needed.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 但与冥想不同，手工活动会产生有形且通常有用的产品，可以增强自尊。我会在手机上保存自己非凡成就的照片，以便在需要时振奋精神。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Since the 1990s, the council has surveyed hundreds of thousands of knitters and crocheters, who routinely list stress relief and creative fulfillment as the activities’ main benefits. Among them is the father of a prematurely born daughter who reported that during the baby’s five weeks in the intensive care unit, “learning how to knit infant hats gave me a sense of purpose during a time that I felt very helpless. It’s a hobby that I’ve stuck with, and it continues to help me cope with stress at work, provide a sense of order in hectic(忙乱的) days, and allow my brain time to solve problems.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 自 20 世纪 90 年代以来，该委员会对数十万编织者和钩编者进行了调查，他们通常将缓解压力和创造性实现列为活动的主要好处。其中一位早产女儿的父亲表示，在婴儿在重症监护室的五周期间，“在我感到非常无助的时候，学习如何编织婴儿帽子给了我一种目标感。这是我一直坚持的一个爱好，它继续帮助我应对工作压力，在忙碌的日子里提供一种秩序感，让我的大脑有时间解决问题。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G. A recent email from the yarn(纺纱) company Red Heart titled “Health Benefits of Crocheting and Knitting” prompted me to explore what else might be known about the health value of activities like knitting. My research revealed that the rewards go well beyond replacing stress and anxiety with the satisfaction of creation.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 最近，纱线公司 Red Heart 发来一封题为“钩编和针织的健康益处”的电子邮件，促使我探索有关针织等活动的健康价值的其他信息。我的研究表明，回报远远超出了用创造的满足感来取代压力和焦虑。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) For example, Karen Hayes, a life coach in Toronto, conducts knitting therapy programs, including Knit to Quit to help smokers give up the habit, and Knit to Heal for people coping with health crises, like a cancer diagnosis or serious illness of a family member. Schools and prisons with craft programs report that they have a calming effect and enhance social skills. And having to follow instructions on complex craft projects can improve children’s math skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 例如，多伦多的生活教练凯伦·海耶斯 (Karen Hayes) 开展编织治疗项目，包括帮助吸烟者戒烟的“编织戒烟”项目，以及为应对健康危机（例如癌症诊断或家庭成员患重病）的人们提供的“编织治愈”项目。设有手工艺项目的学校和监狱报告称，这些项目具有镇静作用并增强社交技能。必须遵循复杂手工项目的说明可以提高孩子的数学技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Some people find that craftwork helps them control their weight. Just as it’s challenging to smoke while knitting, when hands are holding needles and hooks, there’s less snacking and mindless eating out of boredom.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 有些人发现手工艺可以帮助他们控制体重。就像编织时吸烟是一件困难的事情一样，当手拿着针和钩子时，就会减少因无聊而吃零食和无意识地吃东西的情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) I’ve found that my handiwork with yarn has helped my arthritic(患关节炎的) fingers remain more dexterous(灵巧的) as I age. A woman encouraged to try knitting and crocheting after developing an autoimmune disease that caused a lot of hand pain reported on the Craft Yarn Council site that her hands are now less stiff and painful.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 我发现，随着年龄的增长，我用纱线手工制作的东西帮助我患有关节炎的手指保持更加灵巧。一名妇女在患上导致手部严重疼痛的自身免疫性疾病后被鼓励尝试针织和钩编，她在工艺纱线委员会网站上报告说，她的手现在不那么僵硬和疼痛了。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) A 2009 University of British Columbia study of 38 women with an eating disorder who were taught to knit found that learning the craft led to significant improvements. Seventy-four percent of the women said the activity lessened their fears and kept them from thinking about their problem.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 2009 年，不列颠哥伦比亚大学对 38 名患有饮食失调症的女性进行了一项研究，她们在学习编织后发现，学习这门手艺可以带来显着的进步。 74% 的女性表示，这项活动减轻了她们的恐惧，让她们不再思考自己的问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. Betsan Corkhill, a wellness coach in Bath, England, and author of the book Knit for Health & Wellness, established a website, Stitchlinks, to explore the value of what she calls therapeutic knitting. Among her respondents, 54 percent of those who were clinically depressed said that knitting made them feel happy or very happy. In a study of 60 self-selected people with persistent pain, Ms. Corkhill and colleagues reported that knitting enabled them to redirect their focus, reducing their awareness of pain. She suggested that the brain can process just so much at once, and that activities like knitting and crocheting make it harder for the brain to register pain signals. Perhaps most exciting is research that suggests that crafts like knitting and crocheting may help to keep off a decline in brain function with age. In a 2011 study, researchers led Dr. Yonas Geda at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester interviewed a random(随机的) sample of 1,321 people ages 70-89, most of whom were cognitively(在认知方面) normal, about the cognitive activities they engaged in late in life. The study, published in the Journal of Neuropsychiatry & Clinical Neurosciences, found that those who engaged in crafts like knitting and crocheting had a diminished chance of developing mild cognitive disorder and memory loss. M ）Although it is possible that only people who are cognitively healthy would pursue such activities, those who read newspapers or magazines or played music did not show similar benefits. The researchers speculate that craft activities promote the development of nerve pathways in the brain that help to maintain cognitive health.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. Betsan Corkhill 是英国巴斯的一名健康教练，也是《Knit for Health & Wellness》一书的作者，她建立了一个网站 Stitchlinks，以探索她所谓的治疗性针织的价值。在她的受访者中，54% 患有临床抑郁症的人表示，编织让他们感到快乐或非常快乐。 Corkhill 女士及其同事在一项针对 60 名患有持续性疼痛的自选人群的研究中报告说，编织可以帮助他们重新调整注意力，减少对疼痛的意识。她认为大脑一次只能处理这么多事情，而编织和钩编等活动会让大脑更难记录疼痛信号。也许最令人兴奋的是研究表明，针织和钩编等手工艺品可能有助于防止大脑功能随着年龄的增长而下降。在 2011 年的一项研究中，罗切斯特梅奥诊所的 Yonas Geda 博士带领研究人员随机采访了 1,321 名年龄在 70-89 岁之间的人，其中大多数人在认知方面的认知能力正常，了解他们晚年所从事的认知活动。这项发表在《神经精神病学与临床神经科学杂志》上的研究发现，从事编织和钩编等手工艺的人患轻度认知障碍和记忆丧失的机会较小。 M ）虽然可能只有认知健康的人才会从事此类活动，但那些阅读报纸、杂志或演奏音乐的人并没有表现出类似的好处。研究人员推测，手工活动促进大脑神经通路的发育，有助于维持认知健康。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. In support of that suggestion, a 2014 study by Denise C. Park of the University of Texas at Dallas and colleagues demonstrated that learning to knit or do digital photography enhanced memory function in older adults. Those who engaged in activities that were not intellectually challenging either in a social group or alone, did not show such improvements.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 为了支持这一建议，德克萨斯大学达拉斯分校的 Denise C. Park 及其同事在 2014 年进行的一项研究表明，学习编织或进行数码摄影可以增强老年人的记忆功能。那些在社会团体中或单独从事对智力没有挑战性的活动的人，并没有表现出这样的进步。

paragraphs.sourceText: O. Given that sustained social contacts have been shown to support health and a long life, those wishing to maximize the health value of crafts might consider joining a group of like-minded folks. I for one try not to miss a single weekly meeting of my knitting group.
paragraphs.translationZh: O. 鉴于持续的社会接触已被证明有助于健康和长寿，那些希望最大限度地发挥工艺品的健康价值的人可能会考虑加入一群志同道合的人。我尽量不错过我的编织小组的每周一次会议。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36.When the author was a college student, she found that knitting helped her concentrate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36.当作者还是一名大学生时，她发现编织可以帮助她集中注意力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Knitting can help people stay away from tobacco.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 针织可以帮助人们远离烟草。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Even men and children are now joining the army of knitters.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 现在甚至男人和儿童也加入了编织者的大军。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Being a member of a crafts group enhances one’s health and prolongs one’s life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 成为手工艺团体的成员可以增强健康并延长寿命。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Knitting diverts people’s attention from their pain.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 编织可以转移人们对痛苦的注意力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41.The author learnt to knit as a teenager, but it was not until she was much older that she became keenly interested.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41.提交人十几岁的时候就学会了编织，但直到年纪大了才对编织产生了浓厚的兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. When people are knitting, they tend to eat fewer snacks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 当人们编织时，他们往往会吃更少的零食。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Survey findings show that knitting can help people relieve stress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 调查结果显示，编织可以帮助人们缓解压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. According to a study, knitters and crocheters are less likely to suffer mild cognitive damage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 根据一项研究，编织者和钩编者遭受轻度认知损害的可能性较小。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. The products of knitting can increase one’s sense of self-respect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 针织产品可以增加一个人的自尊感。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Nobody really knows how big Lagos is. What’s indisputable is that it’s growing very quic Between now and 2050, the urban population of Africa could triple. Yet cities in sub-Saharan Africa not getting richer the way cities in the rest of the world have. Most urban Africans live in slums(贫民窟); migrants are often not much better off than they were in the countryside. Why?
paragraphs.translationZh: 没有人真正知道拉各斯有多大。无可争议的是，它的增长速度非常快。从现在到 2050 年，非洲的城市人口可能会增加两倍。然而，撒哈拉以南非洲的城市并没有像世界其他地方的城市那样变得更加富裕。大多数非洲城市人生活在贫民窟；移民的境况往往并不比农村好多少。为什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: The immediate problem is poverty. Most of Africa is urbanizing at a lower level of income than other regions of the world did. That means there’s little money around for investment that would make cities liveable and more productive. Without upgrades and new capacity, bridges, roads and power systems are unable to cope with expanding populations. With the exception of South Africa, the only light rail metro system in sub-Saharan Africa is in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Traffic jam leads to expense and unpredictability, things that keep investors away.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当前的问题是贫困。非洲大部分地区正在以低于世界其他地区的收入水平进行城市化。这意味着几乎没有资金可用于使城市变得宜居且生产力更高的投资。如果没有升级和新的容量，桥梁、道路和电力系统就无法应对不断增长的人口。除南非外，撒哈拉以南非洲地区唯一的轻轨地铁系统位于埃塞俄比亚的亚的斯亚贝巴。交通拥堵会带来费用和不可预测性，这些都会让投资者望而却步。

paragraphs.sourceText: In other parts of the world, increasing agricultural productivity and industrialization went together. More productive farmers meant there was a surplus that could feed cities; in turn, that created a pool of labour for factories. But African cities are different. They are too often built around consuming natural resources. Government is concentrated in capitals, so is the money. Most urban Africans work for a small minority of the rich, who tend to be involved in either cronyish(有裙带关系的)businesses or politics. Since African agriculture is still broadly unproductive, food is imported, consuming a portion of revenue.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在世界其他地区，农业生产力的提高和工业化同时进行。农民生产力提高意味着有盈余可以养活城市；反过来，这为工厂创造了劳动力资源。但非洲城市则不同。它们往往是围绕消耗自然资源而建立的。政府集中在首都，金钱也集中在首都。大多数非洲城市人为一小部分富人工作，他们往往参与裙带关系的商业或政治。由于非洲农业仍然普遍生产力低下，粮食依赖进口，消耗了部分收入。

paragraphs.sourceText: So what can be done? Though African countries are poor, not all African cities are. In Lagos, foreign oil workers can pay as much as $ 65,000 per year in rent for a modest apartment in a safe part of town. If that income were better taxed, it might provide the revenue for better infrastructure. If city leaders were more accountable to their residents, they might favour projects designed to help them more. Yet even as new roads are built, new people arrive. When a city’s population grows by 5% a year, it is difficult to keep up.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么可以做什么呢？尽管非洲国家很穷，但并非所有非洲城市都很穷。在拉各斯，外国石油工人每年可以支付高达 65,000 美元的租金，在城镇安全的地方租一套简陋的公寓。如果对这些收入征税更好，它可能会为更好的基础设施提供收入。如果城市领导人对居民更加负责，他们可能会青睐旨在为居民提供更多帮助的项目。然而，即使新的道路建成了，新的人也会到来。当一个城市的人口每年增长 5% 时，就很难跟上。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: For the past several decades, it seems there’s been a general consensus on how to get ahead in America: Get a college education, find a reliable job, and buy your own home. But do Americans still believe in that path, and if they do, is it attainable?
paragraphs.translationZh: 在过去的几十年里，关于如何在美国取得成功似乎已经达成了普遍共识：接受大学教育，找到一份可靠的工作，买自己的房子。但美国人仍然相信这条道路吗？如果他们相信，它可以实现吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: The most recent National Journal poll asked respondents about the American dream, what it takes to achieve their goals, and whether or not they felt a significant amount of control over their ability to be successful. Overwhelmingly, the results show that today, the idea of the American dream—and what it takes to achieve it—looks quite different than it did in the late 20th century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近的《国家杂志》民意调查向受访者询问了美国梦、实现目标所需的条件，以及他们是否感到对自己成功的能力有很大的控制力。压倒性的结果表明，如今美国梦的理念以及实现美国梦所需的条件与 20 世纪末截然不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: By and large, people felt that their actions and hard work—not outside forces—were the deciding factor in how their lives turned out. But respondents had decidedly mixed feelings about what actions make for a better life in current economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 总的来说，人们认为他们的行动和努力工作——而不是外部力量——才是他们生活结果的决定因素。但受访者对于在当前经济形势下哪些行动可以改善生活有着复杂的感受。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the last seven years, Americans have grown more pessimistic about the power of education to lead to success. Even though they see going to college as a fairly achievable goal, a majority—52 percent—think that young people do not need a four-year college education in order to be successful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在过去七年里，美国人对教育带来成功的力量变得更加悲观。尽管他们认为上大学是一个相当可实现的目标，但大多数人（52%）认为年轻人不需要四年制大学教育就能取得成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: Miguel Maeda, 42, who has a master’s degree and works in public health, was the first in his family to go to college, which has allowed him to achieve a sense of financial stability his parents and grandparents never did.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42 岁的米格尔·前田 (Miguel Maeda) 拥有硕士学位，从事公共卫生工作，是家里第一个上大学的人，这让他获得了父母和祖父母从未有过的经济稳定感。

paragraphs.sourceText: While some, like Maeda, emphasized the value of the degree rather than the education itself, others still see college as a way to gain new perspectives and life experiences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管前田等一些人强调学位的价值而不是教育本身，但其他人仍然将大学视为获得新观点和生活体验的一种方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Sixty-year-old Will Fendley, who had a successful career in the military and never earned a college degree, thinks “personal drive” is far more important than just going to college. To Fendley, a sense of drive and purpose, as well as an effective high-school education, and basic life skills, like balancing a checkbook, are the necessary ingredients for a successful life in America.
paragraphs.translationZh: 60 岁的威尔·芬德利 (Will Fendley) 在军队中取得了成功的职业生涯，但从未获得过大学学位，他认为“个人动力”比仅仅上大学重要得多。对芬德利来说，动力和目标感、有效的高中教育以及平衡支票簿等基本生活技能是在美国成功生活的必要要素。
